notes: One document. Main disagreements: (1) phase, where coder B coded most data and disclosure rules as general and coder A as during-work; resolved by tying rules that govern what a user does with AI to during-work and keeping principles, definitions and scope as general. (2) unit_stance, where B coded duties like disclosure and verification as require; resolved to permit (conditions on allowed use) and restrict (narrowing rules), with prohibit for listed uses with no exception. (3) policy_type: P07 scope sentences moved to P61; public-data permission P02->P50; academic-work clause P19->P04 (instructor sets rule); committee roster P84->P80; decision-support sentence P32->P73. (4) Document stance: A permit vs B delegates; resolved permit since the policy sets conditions itself and only one clause defers to instructors. B-only units kept (6): documenting decisions, bias mitigation duty, continuous monitoring, data classification, confidentiality duty, IP infringement. B-only dropped (1): "Transparency is required whenever AI outputs are used", a restatement of the disclosure rule in the same section. A-only unit kept (1): vendor updates bring features into scope.
